object_description: two compact buildings with band-like facades interwoven into the campus
design_condition: The two additions are woven into the existing campus, orient their entrances toward a central public space, and structure a sequence of differentiated outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The two new buildings enhance the campus character and are skilfully interwoven with the existing buildings.

position.rationale: Paired compact volumes are clearly visible and corroborated across the top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The entrances are ideally oriented toward the central public space.

position.rationale: The central gap between the two volumes provides the most plausible entrance orientation.

positive.statement: The outdoor surfaces are harmoniously distributed and well proportioned, creating different spatial atmospheres.

position.rationale: Open areas are distributed around and between the two visible building footprints.

positive.statement: The two-story hall is a surprising architectural added value, while the cascading stairs provide good orientation and visual connections across the floors.

position.rationale: The larger southwest volume contains the most plausible hall and stair zone, though interiors are indistinguishable.

positive.statement: Light is an important element of guidance and also serves the hall, while multiple use independent of school operations is recognizable.

position.rationale: The hall is approximated within the upper portion of the larger visible volume.

positive.statement: The gymnasium organization is practical and naturally and attractively arranged, with clear routes to the cloakrooms and logically placed equipment rooms.

position.rationale: The smaller northeast volume is used as a constrained approximation for the gymnasium.

positive.statement: The band-like facade design is appropriate, robust, and in phase.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal facade bands are directly visible in the elevation views.

positive.statement: The structural and operational strategy suggests an ecologically high-quality facility, with costs slightly below the calculated target average.

position.rationale: Sustainability and cost assessment has no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The locations of the kindergartens and gymnasium are doubtful because of excessive mixing with the existing uses.

position.rationale: The critique concerns program mixing across the paired building masses.

negative.statement: The entrances from the surrounding streets are somewhat poor, one ends in front of the playground, and a southern access to the sports facility is missing.

position.target: surrounding-street entrances and southern sports access
position.rationale: The missing access is anchored to the southern edge and surrounding approach zone.

negative.statement: The required areas for the sports field and playground are not reached.

position.rationale: Required open-space uses are approximated in the exterior area beyond the building footprints.

negative.statement: The nature-experience room and school garden are valuable, but their distance limits their usefulness for school operations.

position.rationale: The distant outdoor-program relationship is approximated at the remote southern-east site edge.

negative.statement: The claim about permeable surfaces is not supported by the plans.

position.rationale: The sustainability claim is not tied to a locatable modeled feature.
